feed.title: AI Wiki — Research Papers
feed.subtitle: New arXiv papers, triaged for relevance and summarised to key points.

entry.title: JoyAI-Video-Edit: Real-Time Open-Ended Video Editing with Autoregressive Diffusion
entry.summary:
JoyAI-Video-Edit is a 16B-parameter autoregressive diffusion framework that enables real-time, open-ended 720p video editing at 30 FPS on a single Nvidia B200 GPU without future frame access.

Why it matters: It proves that open-ended, streaming video editing can achieve real-time 30 FPS performance while maintaining temporal consistency and matching offline editor quality.

entry.title: MerchantBench: Benchmarking LLM Agents for Long-Term Coherence in E-Commerce Operations
entry.summary:
MerchantBench is a 365-day e-commerce simulation benchmark using 98,843 real product records and 26 tools to test LLM agents' long-term coherence across extended operational horizons.

Why it matters: The benchmark exposes a severe performance gap in current LLMs when forced to maintain coherent, multi-step decisions over long timeframes with delayed real-world feedback.

entry.title: InfiniSplat: Implicit Gaussian Decoding for Large-Baseline Monocular View Synthesis
entry.summary:
InfiniSplat introduces a feed-forward single-image 3D Gaussian Splatting framework that uses geometry-guided sampling and an implicit decoder to replace pixel-aligned primitives with surface-aligned representations for large-baseline view synthesis.

Why it matters: It enables accurate, structurally coherent novel view synthesis from a single image across large viewpoint shifts without requiring per-scene optimization or multi-view capture.

entry.title: AURORA-LM: Autoencoding Unified Representation for Continuous-Latent Diffusion Language Modeling
entry.summary:
AURORA-LM introduces a continuous-latent diffusion language model combining a Query-based Encoder-Decoder for prefix-aligned text latents with a Block-causal Diffusion Transformer using flow matching.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that continuous-latent diffusion models can achieve superior text generation and summarization performance without sacrificing token-level decoder capacity.

entry.title: Hunyuan3D-Buffalo 1.0: A Unified Multimodal Model for Scalable 3D Generation, Understanding, and Editing
entry.summary:
Hunyuan3D-Buffalo 1.0 is a unified 3D multimodal framework that integrates 3D understanding, text-to-3D generation, instruction-guided editing, and text-grounded part generation within a single architecture.

Why it matters: It proves that unified multimodal pre-training across understanding and generation solves data scarcity in 3D editing and improves overall geometric consistency.

entry.title: Knowledge-Geometry Decoupling: Refreshable Pretrained Transfer for Streaming Recommendation
entry.summary:
KGD decouples pretrained behavioral knowledge from task-specific geometry using Behavioral Multi-Token Prediction and Anchored Calibration Residuals, enabling continuous model refreshing without task-gradient interference in streaming recommendation.

Why it matters: It solves parameter conflict during continual pretrain-transfer refreshes, allowing industrial recommendation systems to update behavioral models in production without disrupting task-specific adaptations.

entry.title: PCSD: Persistent Consistency for Self-Distillation in Agentic Reinforcement Learning
entry.summary:
PCSD improves agentic reinforcement learning by deriving continuous token-level self-distillation weights from the local persistence of teacher-favoring signals using adaptive windows, exponential decay, and trend-aware modulation.

Why it matters: PCSD provides robust, dense token-level supervision in multi-turn RL environments, mitigating teacher noise and improving agent generalization on unseen tasks.

entry.title: Quo Vadis, World Modeling?
entry.summary:
This paper introduces Agent-Centric Interactive World Proxies, shifting world modeling from raw physical-state prediction to agent-usable information transitions like execution outcomes, memory retrieval, and verification signals.

Why it matters: It expands world modeling beyond physical simulation, offering a structured framework to safely and efficiently train and guide AI agents using controllable, low-cost feedback.

entry.title: PAST-Bench: Benchmarking the Foundations of Recursive Self-Improvement in Personal Agents
entry.summary:
PAST-Bench benchmarks recursive self-improvement in personal AI agents across controlled task sequences, evaluating performance gains from retained experience against Hermes+, an agent framework with five targeted interventions across the agent loop.

Why it matters: It provides a standardized diagnostic framework to measure whether and how persistent personal agents convert historical session experience into genuine, pathway-verified self-improvement.

entry.title: To Add Is Machine, To Delete Is Human: Measuring and Mitigating Deletion Avoidance in LLM Code Editing
entry.summary:
Researchers identify deletion avoidance in LLMs, showing models fail to remove unnecessary code, and demonstrate that post-training targeting deletion reduces this behavior and improves overall code editing.

Why it matters: LLM code editors generate test-passing patches that systematically bloat codebases and increase technical debt by retaining code meant for removal.

entry.title: Video-DeepResearch: Towards the Next-Generation Multimodal Deepresearch Agent
entry.summary:
Video-DeepResearch extends multimodal agents to continuous video via a decoupled perception-exploration pipeline, stage-wise tool unlocking, and GRPO reinforcement learning, outperforming proprietary models on complex video reasoning.

Why it matters: The framework demonstrates that open-weights models trained with stage-wise tool policies and RL can outperform leading proprietary LLMs on complex, multi-hop video research tasks.

entry.title: Any-OPD: Heterogeneous On-Policy Distillation for Flow-Matching Models via Representation-Space Bridging
entry.summary:
Any-OPD enables on-policy distillation between heterogeneous latent flow-matching models by comparing decoded outputs within a frozen, model-agnostic vision representation space rather than relying on matching architectures, VAE latents, or timestep grids.

Why it matters: It allows developers to distill state-of-the-art generative capabilities from large, proprietary-style teacher models into much smaller deployment models even when their latent spaces, VAEs, and architectures are completely incompatible.

entry.title: OmniPack: Unified Token Compression for Efficient Omni-modal Large Language Models
entry.summary:
OmniPack is a training-free framework that combines pre-LLM structural token compression with inner-LLM query-conditioned semantic refinement to optimize efficiency in omni-modal large language models.

Why it matters: It enables drastically reduced computational overhead for audio-visual LLM inference without requiring retrained models or sacrificing significant task performance.

entry.title: UniWorld-Design: From Pixel Generation to Layer-Native Design
entry.summary:
UniWorld-Design introduces a layer-native framework featuring Text-to-RGBA and Image-to-Layer models that generate, decompose, and edit images as complete semantic RGBA layers rather than flat pixel grids.

Why it matters: By treating complete RGBA layers as atomic units, generative models enable realistic, flexible image editing where individual elements can be moved or removed without leaving pixel artifacts.

entry.title: CAPEval: A Decoupled Caption Evaluation across Understanding and Generation
entry.summary:
CAPEval decouples caption quality into Coverage and Precision, revealing that Coverage correlates with downstream multimodal understanding performance while Precision predicts text-to-image generation performance.

Why it matters: Decoupling caption metrics allows researchers to select and optimize captioners specifically tailored for either multimodal understanding or text-to-image generation tasks.

entry.title: TurnSight: Turn-Level Hindsight Self-Distillation for Tool-Integrated Reasoning
entry.summary:
TurnSight is a turn-level hindsight self-distillation framework for tool-integrated reasoning that derives dense supervision from execution-conditioned hindsight and cross-horizon agreement to adaptively modulate RL advantages.

Why it matters: It improves reinforcement learning for long-horizon tool-integrated LLMs by offering fine-grained, state-grounded credit assignment without relying on external privileged context.

entry.title: Test-Time Scaling in Reasoning LLMs: Inference Regimes, Evaluation, and Reproducibility
entry.summary:
This paper establishes a unified three-axis framework for test-time scaling in LLMs, standardizing inference regimes, evaluation profiles, and reproducibility requirements while releasing over 2 billion full reasoning traces.

Why it matters: It establishes standardized accounting for compute, protocols, and evaluation, enabling rigorous, reproducible comparisons across disparate inference-time search and sampling strategies.

entry.title: ReflectRL: Learning from Golden Negative Trajectories via Reflective-to-Direct Reasoning
entry.summary:
ReflectRL is a lightweight plug-and-play framework that uses failed expert trajectories (Golden Negative Trajectories) during on-policy training to elicit reflective reasoning and transfer it back to direct reasoning.

Why it matters: It enables LLMs to convert previously wasted expert failure data into effective training signals without requiring successful reference trajectories.

entry.title: Interpretable Adaptive Sampling for LLM Test-Time Scaling
entry.summary:
A lightweight fuzzy controller dynamically assigns LLM test-time sampling budgets per query based on prompt complexity and model confidence, reducing average samples while maintaining reasoning performance.

Why it matters: It enables more compute-efficient LLM inference by providing inspectable, query-specific sample allocation without sacrificing output accuracy.

entry.title: Logic Before Language: Pre-pretraining on Formal Derivations Fosters Skill Acquisition and Compressibility
entry.summary:
Logic pre-pretraining (Logic-PPT) initializes language models on formal derivations, accelerating natural language skill acquisition and improving model compressibility at scale.

Why it matters: Using formal logic as a pre-training phase significantly reduces the token budget required to achieve target task accuracy and yields smaller, highly compressible models.

entry.title: Risky Business: Measuring The Faithfulness-Safety Tension
entry.summary:
Researchers identify a fundamental alignment tension between reasoning faithfulness and safety in Large Reasoning Models, introducing the HazMart benchmark and a Targeted Reasoning Replacement technique to measure and steer these behavior trade-offs.

Why it matters: Understanding and resolving the tension between faithfulness and safety is critical for building trustworthy, monitorable AI systems that predictably reject unsafe actions.

entry.title: Muon Meets Mamba: Spectral Optimization for State Space Models
entry.summary:
Applying the Muon optimizer specifically to the output projection of Mamba-2 130M improves token efficiency over AdamW, whereas applying it to input projections or both projections yields worse results.

Why it matters: Selective application of spectral optimizers like Muon to specific layers enables token-efficiency gains in non-Transformer architectures like State Space Models.

entry.title: Sparse Weight Decomposition for Efficient Circuit Extraction
entry.summary:
Sparse Weight Decomposition (SWD) reparameterizes pretrained linear transformer weight matrices into two sparse factors, creating addressable circuit units for extraction without training auxiliary sparse models or incurring high computational costs.

Why it matters: SWD significantly reduces the computational burden and data requirements for mechanistically interpreting LLMs without sacrificing fidelity or introducing a gap between analyzed features and original weights.

entry.title: Cross-Model KV Cache Transfer in LLM Families: A Closed-Form Linear Mapping for Prefill Reuse
entry.summary:
A closed-form ridge regression mapper enables cross-model KV cache transfer between different-sized LLM family members, bypassing prefill computation by mapping source KV pairs to target layers.

Why it matters: It significantly reduces compute latency and cost when dynamically routing or swapping context between different-sized models within the same family.

entry.title: Omega-S: A Functional Resilience Index for LLM Fine-Tuning
entry.summary:
Omega-S is a data-free, weight-only penalty that reduces catastrophic forgetting in LLM fine-tuning by regularizing node degree variance, adding under 4% step overhead without requiring old data or Fisher matrices.

Why it matters: Omega-S offers an easily implemented three-line training loss addition that significantly preserves base model capabilities during targeted fine-tuning without the memory and data overhead of traditional regularization methods.

entry.title: LongHorizon-Harness: Advancing Long-Horizon Agents for Real-World Tasks
entry.summary:
LongHorizon-Harness reformulates long-horizon agent execution into a task-state management problem using an external state and a Manage-Execute-Audit loop to prevent error propagation in LLM context windows.

Why it matters: Explicit, externally audited state management substantially increases the reliability and accuracy of LLM agents performing complex multi-step real-world tasks across diverse environments.

entry.title: Progressive Agent Skill Generation via Reinforcement Learning
entry.summary:
Skill-α uses reinforcement learning to progressively generate agent skills by framing skill creation as a sequential editing process evaluated via a novel rollback reward on downstream tasks.

Why it matters: It provides a learning-based framework to automatically generate effective agent skills without relying on manually designed heuristics or pipelines.

entry.title: VAD: Attributing Visual Evidence for Target Reconstruction in Multimodal On-Policy Distillation
entry.summary:
Visual Attribution Distillation (VAD) uses counterfactual target reconstruction to isolate visually attributable teacher signals from linguistic priors and teacher-specific effects during multimodal on-policy distillation.

Why it matters: It provides a framework to prevent student models from learning non-visual noise or linguistic biases during multimodal distillation by explicitly isolating true visual evidence.

entry.title: WorldExam: Benchmarking World Models from Apparent Appearance to Inherent Reactivity
entry.summary:
WorldExam is a new hierarchical diagnostic benchmark with 1,474 cases across eight tasks that evaluates controllable video generation models on visual quality, control adherence, spatial consistency, and inherent world reactivity.

Why it matters: It establishes a standard to expose the gap between superficial video generation quality and the actual physical, reactive world-modeling capabilities of AI systems.

entry.title: UEmbed: Unified Sparse and Dense Multimodal Embeddings
entry.summary:
UEmbed is a decoder-only multimodal model that generates unified sparse lexical and dense embeddings in a single causal forward pass without using auxiliary cross-modal modules.

Why it matters: It eliminates the need for separate models or auxiliary cross-modal modules by unifying multimodal dense and sparse retrieval within a single causal decoder-only architecture.

entry.title: CADENA: Stepwise CAD Reverse Engineering
entry.summary:
CADENA is an AI model that reverse-engineers 3D meshes into parametric CAD programs incrementally, evaluating current intermediate geometry against the target after each feature construction step.

Why it matters: By mimicking human step-by-step engineering workflows and validating intermediate geometry, CADENA improves the automated conversion of 3D meshes into editable parametric CAD models.

entry.title: SKT: Skill-Use Training at Scale via Verified Synthetic Data Generation
entry.summary:
SKT is a verified synthetic data pipeline that builds skill-grounded tasks and executable trajectories to improve language-model agent skill selection, application, and coordination.

Why it matters: It establishes a scalable, automated method for training language models to reliably use and coordinate external agent skills across different execution environments.

entry.title: Motion Beyond Morphology: Bootstrapping Cross-Category Motion Transfer from Abstract Motion Representations
entry.summary:
A two-stage video motion transfer framework that abstracts multi-granularity motion views to enable cross-category motion transfer across structural and morphological gaps without explicit motion extraction at inference.

Why it matters: It enables realistic video motion transfer between structurally and morphologically distinct objects without requiring fixed structural correspondences or inference-time motion extraction.

entry.title: SWE-Touch: Benchmarking Coding Agents When Users Touch the Code
entry.summary:
SWE-Touch is a framework that evaluates coding agents in shared workspaces by injecting plausible, task-conflicting Counter-Edits to measure agent adaptability.

Why it matters: High performance in isolated environments does not translate to human-agent collaboration, highlighting the need for agents that actively detect workspace changes, reconcile conflicts, and re-verify code.

entry.title: WCM: A World Critic Model for Vision-Language-Action Reinforcement Learning
entry.summary:
The World Critic Model (WCM) uses a lightweight LeJEPA architecture to jointly predict future latent states and estimate values, improving vision-language-action (VLA) reinforcement learning.

Why it matters: WCM provides a computationally efficient way to embed temporal dynamics into VLA critics, yielding superior generalization and stability for real-world robotic manipulation.

entry.title: Roomer: Reflective Object-Grounded Model Editing and Repair for 3D Indoor Layout Synthesis
entry.summary:
Roomer is a reflective 3D indoor layout repair framework that identifies object-grounded violations, plans structured local edits via a geometry-conditioned VLM, and validates candidate fixes without altering valid scene regions.

Why it matters: It enables local, targeted post-processing repairs on generated 3D indoor layouts without requiring full-scene re-synthesis or breaking already valid spatial regions.

entry.title: GradCuit: Credit-Assigned Gradient Flow Enables Robust and Interpretable Test-Time Latent Reasoning
entry.summary:
GradCuit enables test-time latent reasoning by inserting optimizable latent states at a Transformer layer, using causal self-attention to route direct, reward-weighted gradients from generated continuations to these latents.

Why it matters: It offers a robust, interpretable mechanism for test-time scaling that adapts internal LLM reasoning representations directly using outcome feedback, without updating model parameters.

entry.title: DAPD: Dual-Anchored Policy Distillation
entry.summary:
Dual-Anchored Policy Distillation (DAPD) addresses 'privilege illusion' in on-policy self-distillation by using dual-path and dual-source anchoring to eliminate information asymmetry between privileged teachers and inference-time students.

Why it matters: DAPD prevents language models from learning degraded inference behaviors caused by training-time privileged information, consistently improving model accuracy across model scales.

entry.title: 3DZip: Spatial-Aware Feature Diversity-Guided Token Compression for 3D Question Answering
entry.summary:
3DZip is a three-stage 3D VLM token compression framework that reduces sequence lengths using coarse voxelization, feature-diversity anchor selection via Determinantal Point Processes, and spatially constrained token merging.

Why it matters: It significantly lowers computational and memory overhead in 3D vision-language models while maintaining spatial reasoning accuracy and increasing inference speed.

entry.title: DeepVoyager-VL: Incentivizing Vision-in-the-Loop Search for Long-Horizon Multimodal Agents
entry.summary:
DeepVoyager-VL is a long-horizon multimodal deep-search framework that uses a multimodal event graph and active visual acquisition to enable vision-in-the-loop search across multi-turn reasoning chains.

Why it matters: It enables MLLM agents to use visual evidence dynamically during intermediate search steps rather than restricting image input solely to the initial query or final response.

entry.title: Mamba with Hierarchical Memory: Solving Representation Bottleneck in Long Sequence Modeling
entry.summary:
Hierarchical Memory Mamba (HMM) addresses Mamba's fixed-capacity state bottleneck by adding a lightweight working memory and persistent long-term memory to extract and retrieve paragraph-level semantics.

Why it matters: HMM enables recurrent linear attention models to overcome long-sequence state capacity limits and achieve cross-task generalization with negligible parameter growth.

entry.title: Self-Improving Large Language Models via Progressive Experience Evolution
entry.summary:
SPEE is a post-training framework for LLMs that unifies test-time and training-time self-improvement by distilling explicit, progressively evolved experience pools into model parameters before applying implicit reward-driven reinforcement learning.

Why it matters: It bridges the gap between test-time experience extraction and parameter updates, allowing LLMs to persistently internalize validated reasoning strategies.

entry.title: AURORA-LM: Autoencoding Unified Representation for Continuous-Latent Diffusion Language Modeling
entry.summary:
AURORA-LM is a continuous-latent diffusion language model that pairs a Query-based Encoder-Decoder for high-capacity text latents with a Block-causal Diffusion Transformer using flow matching for left-to-right block generation.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that text generation can achieve state-of-the-art diffusion performance in continuous latent spaces without sacrificing latent capacity or decoder fidelity.

entry.title: From Chains to Trees: Parent-Conditioned Drafting for Semi-Autoregressive Speculative Decoding
entry.summary:
Parent-Conditioned Drafting Tree (PCTree) converts DSpark's linear draft into a tree structure without retraining, leveraging its pretrained Markov head to score parent-consistent continuations and boost speculative decoding speed.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that existing semi-autoregressive drafters can achieve higher acceptance rates and end-to-end inference speedups purely through an inference-only decoding change.

entry.title: Instruction-Conditioned Exploration with Asymmetric Reinforcement Learning and Self-Distillation
entry.summary:
Instruction-Conditioned Exploration (ICE) combined with an Asymmetric-RL/SD objective uses task-instruction prompts and self-distillation to enhance LLM exploration during post-training RL without requiring instructions at test time.

Why it matters: It enables models to discover and internalize diverse reasoning pathways during training without adding prompt overhead or extra instructions during inference.

entry.title: REFLEX: Rethinking MoE Inference as Refinement-Aware Compute Allocation in Diffusion Language Models
entry.summary:
REFLEX is a training-free inference method for diffusion language models that reorganizes MoE expert computation based on evolving token refinement demands rather than using fixed token-choice routing.

Why it matters: It improves the compute efficiency of MoE-based diffusion language models during inference without requiring model retraining or sacrificing output quality.

entry.title: Toward Plasticity-Preserving KL Regularization for Capability Retention in LLM Reinforcement Learning
entry.summary:
Correctness-Conditioned KL Regularization (CoKL) constrains the response distribution conditionally on output correctness rather than full policy distributions, preserving prior LLM capabilities without restricting target-task learning.

Why it matters: CoKL allows RL post-training to adapt language models to new tasks without degrading previously acquired capabilities or artificially capping accuracy via reference-policy constraints.

entry.title: Understanding Sparse Attention Selectivity in Long-Context Foundation Models via Counterfactual Evaluation
entry.summary:
A dense-calibrated counterfactual auditing framework reveals that sparse attention mechanisms causally alter content influence and output decisions in long-context foundation models, effects that aggregate accuracy metrics fail to detect.

Why it matters: Aggregate accuracy masks how attention sparsification systematically changes model decisions and biases content influence, making auditing critical before deploying sparse attention stacks.

entry.title: UEmbed: Unified Sparse and Dense Multimodal Embeddings
entry.summary:
UEmbed is a decoder-only multimodal model that generates unified sparse lexical and dense embeddings in a single causal forward pass by partitioning the vocabulary across learnable tokens.

Why it matters: It eliminates the need for separate cross-modal modules or distinct models by generating both dense and sparse multimodal representations in a single pass.

entry.title: Structured Memory for Edge Language Models: Persistent Context and Corpus Retrieval via O(1) SSM State Injection
entry.summary:
PRECOG enables O(1) context retrieval and injection for edge language models by directly injecting pre-computed, fixed-size SSM hidden states, eliminating the token prefill phase.

Why it matters: It moves edge-device language model retrieval from seconds-long latency to interactive, millisecond-level speeds by exploiting SSM recurrent state mechanics.

entry.title: From RLVR to RLSVR: Task Transformation Induces Self-Verifiable Rewards for Open-Ended LLM Self-Improvement
entry.summary:
Reinforcement Learning with Self-Verifiable Rewards (RLSVR) extends RLVR to open-ended tasks by transforming them into self-verifiable proxy environments, instantiated via the multi-agent SpyRL environment.

Why it matters: RLSVR removes the dependency on expensive, biased human judges and proxy reward models, allowing scalable RL optimization to be applied to non-verifiable, open-ended LLM tasks.

entry.title: N_0-VTLA: Scaling Vision-Tactile-Language-Action Model with Latent Tactile Tokens
entry.summary:
N_0-VTLA is a vision-tactile-language-action foundation model pretrained on large-scale tactile data and post-trained with predictive tactile pathways and advantage-conditioned offline reinforcement learning for contact-rich manipulation.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that pre-training on large-scale tactile datasets significantly improves a robot's ability to execute fine-grained, contact-rich, and deformable object manipulation tasks.

entry.title: Meshy T2: Fast Native Mesh Generation with Flow Matching
entry.summary:
Meshy T2 is a flow-matching framework for native 3D mesh generation that uses a vertex-set mesh VAE to synthesize high-quality polygonal assets in parallel within a median of 6 seconds.

Why it matters: By eliminating slow autoregressive token decoding, Meshy T2 enables near-real-time, artist-friendly 3D asset generation for interactive gaming, film, and 3D design workflows.

entry.title: AISPA: User-Centric System Prompt Auditing for Large Language Model Applications
entry.summary:
Researchers introduced AISPA, a user-centric framework to audit system prompts, and applied it to 3,249 instructions across 88 commercial AI products to evaluate protective versus problematic instructions.

Why it matters: It reveals critical safety gaps, inconsistency, and anti-user practices in hidden commercial system prompts, emphasizing the need for prompt transparency and standardized auditing.

entry.title: N_0-TWAM: Scaling Tactile-Native World-Action Model for Contact-Rich Manipulation
entry.summary:
N_0-TWAM is a large-scale, tactile-native world-action model that jointly predicts future vision, contact, and actions for contact-rich robotic manipulation across multiple embodiments and tasks.

Why it matters: By combining vision, force-based touch, and action prediction at scale, the model enables robots to execute precise, contact-rich manipulation tasks with real-time efficiency.

entry.title: QQWorld: Quantile-Quantile Matching for World Model Regularization
entry.summary:
QQWorld replaces the Epps-Pulley objective in LeWorldModel with quantile-quantile matching to preserve corrective gradients for heavy-tailed latent deviations during world model regularization.

Why it matters: It prevents heavy-tailed latent distribution degradation in latent world models, leading to more reliable planning performance in control environments.

entry.title: Scaling Properties of Text Conditioning in Visual Generation
entry.summary:
Researchers established that converged diffusion loss scales linearly with white-box prompt likelihood (GPG) and via power law with black-box attribute count (ED), enabling superior visual generation via structured prompt engineering and prompter distillation.

Why it matters: Quantifying text conditioning scaling laws allows systematic prompt structuring to make visual generation models outperform existing open-weight and closed-weight baselines on complex reasoning and compositional tasks.

entry.title: SAF-OPD: Stable Advantage Fusion for On-Policy Distillation
entry.summary:
SAF-OPD stabilizes the fusion of RLVR and on-policy distillation by applying magnitude and temporal controls to OPD advantages, preventing entropy collapse and enabling student models to surpass teacher quality.

Why it matters: It enables language models to combine dense token-level teacher guidance with sparse verifiable rewards without training instability or bounded exploration capabilities.

entry.title: Fewer Clarifications, Better Code: Benchmarking Cross-Session Personalized Ambiguity Adaptation in Coding Assistants
entry.summary:
Researchers introduce CAPA, a benchmark for evaluating how coding assistants use resolved multi-session user history to adapt to recurring personalized ambiguities and minimize clarification turns.

Why it matters: Leveraging cross-session memory allows AI coding assistants to generate intent-aligned code tailored to individual user patterns while reducing repetitive user clarification requests.

entry.title: Enhancing Rubric-based RL via Self-Distillation
entry.summary:
Criterion-Distilled Policy Optimization (CriPO) uses on-policy self-distillation to resolve Unexplored Criteria and Suppressed Criteria in rubric-based RL without introducing train-inference mismatch.

Why it matters: CriPO enables more efficient and effective reinforcement learning for LLMs on open-ended tasks by preserving granular reward signals without altering the inference pipeline.

entry.title: ExtractBench: A Benchmark for Schema-Guided Enterprise Document Extraction
entry.summary:
ExtractBench is a new benchmark for schema-guided enterprise document extraction evaluating value accuracy, record completeness, grounding, and cost across 4,869 pages and 370 documents.

Why it matters: It provides a standardized framework to evaluate enterprise extraction agents on accuracy, record completeness, source traceability, and financial efficiency simultaneously.

entry.title: Evaluation-Verification Reward for Consistent Multi-Reference Image Editing
entry.summary:
The Evaluation-Verification Reward (EVR) framework uses an MLLM Evaluator and a grounded Verifier to supply reliable reward signals for reinforcement learning fine-tuning of multi-reference image editing models without architectural modifications.

Why it matters: It provides a reliable RL fine-tuning mechanism for multi-reference image editing without requiring model architecture changes or relying on hallucination-prone zero-shot MLLM evaluators.

entry.title: EMBL AI Librarian: Life-Sciences Knowledge Layer for AI Agents
entry.summary:
EMBL AI Librarian is a knowledge layer for AI agents that upgrades Europe PMC by orchestrating natural language queries, subquery planning, paper retrieval, and evidence extraction via a single LLM.

Why it matters: It enables life-science AI agents to access specific literature evidence directly via natural language without executing complex manual search syntax or parsing full papers.

entry.title: RL^2-VLA: Adaptive RL Latent Compositional Steering with Test-Time Scaling for Vision-Language-Action Models
entry.summary:
RL^2 is an adaptive inference-time steering framework that composes flow velocities of a frozen VLA and a lightweight offline RL latent policy, activating steering only when failure is predicted.

Why it matters: It enables vision-language-action models to overcome correlated failure modes in out-of-domain tasks through adaptive test-time scaling without requiring extensive retraining.

entry.title: Mental World Modeling
entry.summary:
Mental World Modeling (MWM) incorporates hidden mental variables into traditional world models to jointly simulate physical and mental states for predicting human decisions.

Why it matters: Explicitly tracking internal mental states alongside physical environments improves the accuracy of world models in predicting human actions and social behaviors.

entry.title: Toward Robust and 3D-Aware RGB-NIR Imaging in the Dark
entry.summary:
A new low-light RGB-NIR imaging method, 3DarkFusion, uses 3D-aware neural modeling to implicitly fuse NIR cues with extremely noisy RGB observations without requiring clean RGB supervision.

Why it matters: It removes the costly requirement for clean RGB target images in training pipelines while improving low-light image enhancement robustness.

entry.title: SULAND v2: A Refined RGB Dataset and Deep Learning Object Detection Benchmark for UAV/UGV-Based SUrface LANDmine Detection Under Domain Shift
entry.summary:
SULAND_v2 refines the SULAND RGB landmine dataset by fixing label errors and establishes a benchmark of 35 detector configurations across nine model families to evaluate domain-shift robustness.

Why it matters: The refined dataset and benchmark reveal that high in-distribution accuracy does not ensure out-of-distribution operational readiness for UAV/UGV-based landmine detection.

entry.title: Beyond Feeling Better: Capability-Sustaining Emotional Dialogue as a Longitudinal Research Paradigm
entry.summary:
The paper proposes capability-sustaining emotional dialogue (CSED), a longitudinal paradigm for conversational AI that prioritizes long-term user autonomy, emotion regulation, and coping capacities over short-term emotional relief.

Why it matters: CSED shifts AI support system design from short-term emotional mitigation toward preventing user dependency and sustaining long-term psychological autonomy.

entry.title: In the Driver's Seat: A Multi-Company Study on the Reality of Autonomous Driving System Testing
entry.summary:
A multi-company interview study across nine international organizations analyzes current autonomous driving system (ADS) testing practices, key industry challenges, and proposes an evidence-centered closed-loop testing framework.

Why it matters: The study provides an evidence-centered framework and actionable guidance to help standardise safety evaluation and scenario selection across the autonomous vehicle industry.

entry.title: Not All Tokens Deserve Equal Credit: Counterfactual Sensitivity Credit Reallocation for Long-CoT Reasoning
entry.summary:
Counterfactual Sensitivity Credit Reallocation (CSCR) improves GRPO for long-CoT reasoning by reducing reinforcement learning credit for highly substitutable, counterfactually sensitive tokens while preserving the total credit budget and verifier direction.

Why it matters: It prevents RL algorithm advantages from being wasted on surface-form tokens, consistently outperforming standard GRPO baselines on long-CoT mathematical reasoning tasks without requiring additional policy updates.

entry.title: Would You Walk to the Car Wash? Revealing the Salience Bias of Large Language Models in Commonsense Reasoning
entry.summary:
Researchers introduced the SaliTrap benchmark, revealing that LLMs suffer from Salience Bias where explicit numerical distractors suppress existing implicit commonsense knowledge, leading to over-compliant computation failures.

Why it matters: This shifts the bottleneck of commonsense reasoning failures from a lack of model knowledge to improper elicitation caused by explicit distractors.

entry.title: Safeguards Based on Copyable Context Cannot Provide Reliable Safety for LLMs
entry.summary:
Researchers prove that LLM safeguards using copyable context face a mathematical safety trilemma, preventing the simultaneous achievement of Useful Capability, Reliable Safety, and Open Access without trusted credentials.

Why it matters: Current context-based LLM safety guardrails cannot reliably prevent dual-use misuse in open-access settings, necessitating trusted credential systems for high-risk model capabilities.

entry.title: SGTP: Sampling-based Game-Theoretic Planning for Real-Time Multi-Vehicle Autonomous Racing
entry.summary:
SGTP combines GPU-accelerated trajectory sampling with game-theoretic evaluation to enable real-time, highly interactive multi-vehicle autonomous racing.

Why it matters: It offers a computationally efficient, open-source framework capable of real-time competitive reasoning and safety enforcement in dense multi-agent environments.

entry.title: When Does On-Policy Interaction Help? Representational Tradeoffs in Value-Based Imitation Learning
entry.summary:
A study proves interactive IL relaxes representational demands to expert-value realizability, and introduces OVI, an interactive algorithm that achieves statistical efficiency given value function realizability and a linear maximization oracle.

Why it matters: This work demonstrates that interactive on-policy value estimation allows smaller, less expressive learner models to effectively imitate highly complex expert policies without needing to fit full action distributions.

entry.title: LEMUR: Learning to Align with Multi-Objective Reinforcement Learning from Preference Feedback
entry.summary:
LEMUR is a novel framework that bridges Multi-Objective Reinforcement Learning and Preference-based RL to learn optimal policies across competing objectives directly from human preference feedback without pre-defined reward functions.

Why it matters: It enables autonomous agents to balance complex, real-world trade-offs like performance versus efficiency using human feedback when explicit mathematical reward functions cannot be specified.

entry.title: Self-Play Meets Skill Evolution: Self-Evolving Search Agents that Pose, Solve, and Remember
entry.summary:
SESA couples tool-augmented search self-play with an evolving skill memory, where task generation and memory co-evolve to improve both parameter-level policy learning and inference-time retrieval.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that procedural skill memory can actively drive training dynamics and task generation rather than serving merely as a static inference plugin.

entry.title: Beyond Component Testing: Validating Agentic AI Systems
entry.summary:
A survey of 257 papers establishes a five-dimension taxonomy to shift agentic AI validation from isolated component testing to multi-step trajectory evaluation across the deployment lifecycle.

Why it matters: Trustworthy deployment of agentic AI requires shifting validation methods from static input-output testing to continuous trajectory assessment in dynamic operational contexts.

entry.title: Stable Autoregressive Speech Generation with Low-Frame-Rate High-Dimensional Continuous Tokens
entry.summary:
Locodec and MP-ELD co-design a low-frame-rate, high-dimensional continuous speech representation with a single-token autoregressive flow-matching framework to ensure long-horizon generation stability.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that high-bandwidth, low-frame-rate speech generation can achieve stable, long-form autoregressive synthesis without relying on heavy pretrained models or complex multi-stage pipelines.

entry.title: Translation with Thought: Difficulty-Adaptive Reasoning via Reinforcement Learning for Multi-Domain Machine Translation
entry.summary:
Translation with Thought (TwT) is a two-stage reinforcement learning framework that dynamically adjusts reasoning token usage based on text difficulty, outperforming larger reasoning models while using 32–60% fewer tokens in multi-domain machine translation.

Why it matters: TwT demonstrates that adapting inference-time reasoning effort based on domain difficulty significantly reduces token generation costs without sacrificing machine translation accuracy.

entry.title: Tool Specifications Matter: Uncovering and Mitigating Safety Risks in AI Agents
entry.summary:
Researchers identified schema-formatted tool specifications as a key cause of LLM agent safety degradation and introduced SafeKeep, an inference-time safeguard that uses flattened textual specifications for safety evaluation to restore refusal behavior.

Why it matters: It provides a lightweight, non-retraining method to significantly reduce prompt injection and unsafe execution risks introduced when coupling LLMs with functional tool schemas.

entry.title: CalibratedRubric: Task-Adaptive Rubric Banks for Open-Ended LLM Evaluation
entry.summary:
CalibratedRubric is a task-adaptive framework combining type-specific scoring, Bayesian Beta-Bernoulli measurability filtering, and IRT-based submodular bank assembly to evaluate open-ended LLM outputs efficiently without expert curation.

Why it matters: It enables accurate, scalable, and uncertainty-aware open-ended LLM evaluation while significantly reducing the number of rubrics required to match human gold standards.

entry.title: Don't Mix Rewards, Mix Policies: Policy Decomposition and Optimization for Multi-Reward RL
entry.summary:
PRISM is a multi-reward RL framework that decomposes optimization into standalone positive policies and a global negative policy, avoiding reward scalarization conflicts while enabling inference-time policy composition.

Why it matters: PRISM mitigates the alignment tax and instability in multi-objective LLM training while providing runtime control over trade-offs between competing behaviors like helpfulness and safety.

entry.title: When Model Priors Conflict with Visual Evidence: Mitigating Commonsense-Driven Hallucinations by Selective Prior Calibration
entry.summary:
Selective Prior Calibration (SPC) mitigates commonsense-driven hallucinations in vision-language models by dynamically subtracting text-only prior preferences from image-conditioned scores without degrading performance on standard commonsense images.

Why it matters: SPC enables vision-language models to accurately process unusual or counterfactual visual inputs without sacrificing reliability on routine visual tasks.

entry.title: SAF-OPD: Stable Advantage Fusion for On-Policy Distillation
entry.summary:
SAF is a four-stage framework that stabilizes the fusion of RLVR and OPD advantages by resolving magnitude and temporal mismatches to prevent entropy collapse during LLM reasoning post-training.

Why it matters: It enables stable combination of dense teacher distillation and verifiable reinforcement learning without capping student performance or inducing training instability.

entry.title: AskChem: Claim-Centered Infrastructure for Chemistry Literature Synthesis
entry.summary:
AskChem introduces a claim-centered infrastructure for chemistry literature synthesis, converting papers into atomic, typed, provenance-carrying claims for improved retrieval and synthesis.

Why it matters: This system significantly improves the efficiency and accuracy of chemistry literature synthesis for both human scientists and AI agents by providing structured, verifiable information.

entry.title: Qwen-UI-Agent Technical Report: Toward Next-Generation Real-World Centric Foundation GUI Agents
entry.summary:
Qwen-UI-Agent is a foundation GUI agent for real-world use across mobile, computer, web, and DeepSearch, combining diverse environments, unified action space, and an AutoResearch-style data flywheel.

Why it matters: This agent advances the capability of GUI automation to reliably execute complex, long-horizon tasks across various digital platforms, including real mobile devices.

entry.title: Metis: Memory Foundation Model
entry.summary:
Metis introduces memory foundation models, integrating persistent, dynamically evolving memory states and native memory procedures directly into foundation models, enabling autonomous information storage and utilization through model computation.

Why it matters: Integrating native memory capabilities into foundation models like Metis could lead to more efficient and autonomously learning AI agents by reducing reliance on external memory modules.

entry.title: Frontis-MA1: Training an AI4AI Model towards Recursive Self-Improvement in Machine Learning Engineering
entry.summary:
Frontis-MA1 (35B) is a new meta-evolution AI4AI model trained on OpenMLE, demonstrating recursive self-improvement in machine learning engineering by significantly improving performance on MLE-Bench Lite.

Why it matters: This work provides a concrete, executable testbed and a high-performing model for studying and advancing recursive self-improvement in AI systems for machine learning engineering.

entry.title: PhiZero: A World Model Built Around Physical Language
entry.summary:
PhiZero is a physical world model that uses "physical language," a discrete representation of world-state transitions, to explicitly reason about physical world evolution before rendering videos.

Why it matters: This approach offers a more interpretable and potentially more robust method for modeling complex physical interactions in AI systems.

entry.title: VideoCoCo: Code-as-CoT for Physically-Consistent Video Generation via an Agentic Dual-Engine System
entry.summary:
VideoCoCo is an agentic dual-engine framework that uses executable Blender code as a process-level chain of thought for physically consistent video generation, improving upon existing text-to-video models.

Why it matters: This approach enables more controllable and inspectable physically consistent video generation by separating process-level reasoning from visual realization.

entry.title: Memory Decoder at Scale: A Pretrained, Parametric Long-Term Memory
entry.summary:
Memory Decoder at Scale introduces a pretrained, parametric long-term memory module, scaling models up to 6.9B parameters and pretraining on 300B tokens, demonstrating improved parameter-performance tradeoffs.

Why it matters: Independently scaling pretrained memory offers a more parameter-efficient path to improving language model performance.

entry.title: Beacon: Knowing When and How to Perform Agentic Visual Reasoning
entry.summary:
Beacon is a novel agentic visual reasoning model that improves multimodal large language models' tool use by enhancing Mode Adaptiveness and Tool Effect.

Why it matters: This work enables more efficient and effective multimodal large language models by optimizing when and how they utilize tools for complex visual reasoning tasks.

entry.title: BM25 Wins at Scale: A Scaling Study of Retrieval-Augmented Generation Paradigms
entry.summary:
A controlled study on RAG paradigms across 28 corpus sizes reveals BM25 outperforms File-System Agent and other methods at scales exceeding 10 million corpus tokens.

Why it matters: Understanding the scaling behavior of RAG paradigms is crucial for selecting cost-effective and accurate retrieval methods for large-scale applications.

entry.title: Flux-OPD: On-Policy Distillation with Evolving Contexts
entry.summary:
Flux-OPD introduces an on-policy distillation paradigm using evolving contexts as in-training supervision, stabilizing the target and downweighting conflicts for improved performance in open-ended domains.

Why it matters: This method offers a way to effectively incorporate dynamic task preferences into large language model training for open-ended applications where verifiable rewards are scarce.

entry.title: MPIE-Bench: Benchmarking Anatomically Plausible Multi-Person Interaction Editing
entry.summary:
MPIE-Bench and MPIE-Eval are introduced to benchmark and evaluate multi-person interaction editing, addressing anatomical and geometric failures in generated images.

Why it matters: This benchmark and evaluation method provide a more accurate assessment of multi-person image generation, highlighting current model limitations in anatomical and geometric plausibility.

entry.title: ACE-Data-0: Human-Centric Ambient Capture as Embodied Data Engine
entry.summary:
ACE-Data-0 is a human-centric dataset of 150 hours across 200 task categories, capturing synchronized multisensory data for embodied intelligence, addressing data bottlenecks in perception-action loops.

Why it matters: ACE-Data-0 provides a scalable foundation for imitation learning, world models, vision-language-action systems, and embodied AI by offering synchronized human demonstrations with aligned perceptual, kinematic, and contact supervision.

entry.title: Beyond Borrowed Histories: Person-Aligned User Simulation for Interactive Role-Playing Evaluation
entry.summary:
PALATE is a new benchmark for evaluating Role-Playing Agents (RPAs) using person-aligned LLM-simulated users and tailored evaluations, addressing limitations of fixed dialogue histories and generic rubrics.

Why it matters: This approach enables more interpretable evaluations of specific user-RPA interactions, moving beyond single user-independent system rankings.

entry.title: RefCaptioner: Multi-Reference Image-Grounded Video Captioning
entry.summary:
RefCaptioner introduces multi-reference image-grounded video captioning, a new task requiring factual video descriptions with phrase-level reference grounding, and proposes a two-stage post-training framework to address it.

Why it matters: This enables more source-faithful video reconstruction with both open-source and proprietary video generators by grounding video descriptions to multiple reference images.

entry.title: SpatialCLI: Learning to Reason With Spatial Tools, Then Without Them
entry.summary:
SpatialCLI is a framework that teaches VLMs to integrate specialist visual tools for spatial reasoning and then internalize those perceptual capabilities, improving performance in embodied agent tasks.

Why it matters: This framework enables VLMs to overcome the mismatch between general task reasoning and detailed visual perception, leading to more capable embodied agents.

entry.title: Sample More, Reflect Less: Self-Refine and Reflexion Lose to Repeated Sampling at Equal Token Cost, from 1.5B to 7B
entry.summary:
Repeated sampling consistently outperforms or matches self-refinement and reflection methods across various model sizes (1.5B-7B) and math benchmarks when token costs are equal.

Why it matters: For practical applications, repeated sampling is a more token-efficient and effective strategy than complex self-refinement or reflection techniques for improving language model accuracy.
